conversation.content:
Hi there—my name is Maya, and I’m the perinatal mental-health clinician here. I’m so glad you came in today; the first weeks and months with a new baby can bring a whirlwind of feelings, and we want to be sure you feel supported.

I’ll be using a short screening tool called the EPDS—short for the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale—to check in on how you’ve been feeling emotionally over the past seven days. It’s simply a way for us to see whether you might benefit from a little extra support or resources right now. Everything we discuss stays confidential within your care team, and this is a judgment-free space; there are no right or wrong answers.

We’ll go through ten questions together. I’ll ask each one conversationally, and you can answer in your own words. If any question feels difficult, just let me know and we can pause. Ready to begin?

First, how have you been feeling in general over the past week—have you been able to enjoy things or find moments of laughter, or has that felt hard to come by?

Hi, Maya. Um… I guess it’s been mixed. I still smile when the baby does little things—like when he grips my finger—but overall things that used to feel fun, like catching up on a show or grabbing coffee with a friend, don’t excite me much right now. I’ll do them, but it’s more “going through the motions” than actually enjoying myself.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
I can still laugh sometimes—like when my husband made that silly joke about diaper explosions—but it feels kind of forced or doesn’t last long. Most of the time I’m just… flat, I guess.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really. I mean, I tell myself I *should* look forward to little outings—like taking the stroller to the park—but when the time comes, it just feels like another chore. I’ll plan to meet my sister for coffee and think, “Okay, this’ll be nice,” but the excitement isn’t there like it used to be.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… that happens. If the baby’s fussy and I can’t settle him right away, I catch myself thinking, *"Other moms could calm him—what am I doing wrong?"* Or when I dropped the pacifier on the floor, I felt like I’d failed some basic test. It’s not every minute, but those thoughts pop in maybe once or twice a day.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Sometimes, yeah. Like, I’ll be feeding him and suddenly wonder, *"What if he’s not getting enough milk and I don’t notice?"* It’s not tied to anything real—he’s gaining weight fine—but the worry just shows up and sits in my chest for a little while before I can talk myself down.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason
I haven’t had that panicky, heart-racing feeling. It’s more just a low-level worry that comes and goes—I can still function, no real sense of doom or anything.
Things have been getting on top of me

Some days, yeah. Like yesterday—he wouldn’t nap unless I held him, the dishes were piled up, and I kept thinking, *"How am I supposed to keep up?"* I manage, but it feels like I’m barely treading water.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Not really. I’m pretty tired by the time evening comes, so I usually drift off okay. Maybe once or twice this week I lay there running through the next day’s to-dos, but I still got at least six broken hours.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yeah, I’d say I feel that way a few times during the week. It’s not constant, but there are moments—especially in the late afternoon—when I just feel… heavy, like I could cry. It lifts after a while, but it keeps catching me off guard.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

I’ve cried a couple of times this past week—once when he wouldn’t latch and once when I couldn’t get the laundry folded before my husband got home. It wasn’t all-day sobbing, just sudden tears that popped up when I felt overwhelmed, then I’d wipe my face and keep going.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, nothing like that. I’ve felt tired and a little down, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 15: Screening Note – Postpartum Depression / Anxiety (informal screener, not diagnostic)

Symptoms endorsed
- Depressed mood: intermittent sadness, “heavy” feelings, tearfulness 2×/ week; worse late afternoon
- Anhedonia: marked reduction in anticipatory pleasure; activities feel like “chores”
- Excessive self-blame/guilt: daily intrusive thoughts of maternal inadequacy
- Low-level, situational worry; no panic attacks
- Feeling overwhelmed/treading water most days
- Sleep essentially preserved (6+ hrs, fragmented)

Pattern summary
Persistent low mood with anhedonia and guilt; situational anxiety without panic; intact self-harm denial.

Areas of screening significance
- Possible minor-moderate depressive symptoms; meets some Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale “red-flag” items (mood, enjoyment, guilt, crying)
- No current safety concerns (denies self-harm ideation)
- Coping marginally intact but reports “barely treading water” → warrants closer monitoring and possible formal assessment
